# LinkedIn Profile Search By Name scraper (No Cookies)

The Apify actor [`harvestapi/linkedin-profile-search-by-name`](https://apify.com/harvestapi/linkedin-profile-search-by-name) as typed Telo kinds, generated from its default build **0.0.55** (module version **0.1.0**). Runs use whatever build the actor has as default when they start, so they keep working as Apify retires old builds; the input types below are refreshed weekly and can lag an actor that changed its input since.

Search for LinkedIn profiles by name with filters and extract detailed profile information, including work experience, education history, location and more. No cookies or account required.

## Pricing

Pay per event — Search page results $0.004, Full profile $0.004, Full profile + email search $0.01, Main profile $0.002 (Free-plan prices; paid plans pay less). Cap the spend with `maxTotalChargeUsd`.

Runs are charged to the Apify account whose token the `ApifyClient` holds. See the [Store page](https://apify.com/harvestapi/linkedin-profile-search-by-name) for current prices.

## Usage

```yaml
kind: Actor.ApifyClient
metadata: { name: apify }
token: !cel "secrets.apifyToken"
---
kind: Actor.Run          # or Actor.Start for runs longer than 5 minutes
metadata: { name: scrape }
client: !ref apify
maxTotalChargeUsd: 1     # optional: timeout, memory, maxItems, maxTotalChargeUsd
---
kind: Run.Sequence
metadata: { name: main }
steps:
  - name: scrape
    invoke: !ref scrape
    inputs:
      profileScraperMode: "Short"
```

- **`Run`** calls Apify's synchronous endpoint and returns `{ items }`. Apify holds the request open for at most 300 seconds; a longer run fails with HTTP 408.
- **`Start`** starts the run, long-polls it until it finishes, and returns `{ run, items }`. A run that ends `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT` or `ABORTED` raises `APIFY_RUN_NOT_SUCCEEDED` with the run as `data`.

## Input

Only these fields are accepted — `telo check` rejects any other.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `profileScraperMode` | string | yes |  | Profile Scraper Mode — Choose the mode for scraping LinkedIn profiles. The Short mode provides basic information, while the Full mode includes full detailed profile data. |
| `firstName` | string |  |  | First Name — First name of the person to search for. |
| `lastName` | string |  |  | Last Name — Last name of the person to search for. |
| `strictSearch` | boolean |  | `true` | Strict Search — Enabling strict search will ensure that only profiles matching both the first and last names exactly are returned. |
| `maxPages` | integer |  |  | Maximum number of pages to scrape — Maximum number of pages to scrape for each query. The actor will stop scraping when this limit is reached. |
| `locations` | array |  |  | Locations Filter — Filter Profiles by these LinkedIn locations. Example: `San Francisco`. LinkedIn does not always understand your text queries. For example for "UK" query it will apply "Ukraine" location, so you should use "United Kingdom" in this case. Try this out first in the location filter inp |
| `currentCompanies` | array |  |  | Current Company Filter — Filter Profiles by these LinkedIn companies. Provide full LinkedIn URLs |
| `pastCompanies` | array |  |  | Past Company Filter — Filter Profiles by these LinkedIn past companies. Provide full LinkedIn URLs |
| `schools` | array |  |  | School Filter — Filter Profiles by these LinkedIn schools. Example: `Stanford University`. |
| `currentJobTitles` | array |  |  | Current Job Title Filter (exact search) — Filter Profiles by these LinkedIn current job titles. Example: `Software Engineer`. |
| `industryIds` | array |  |  | Industry IDs Filter — Filter Profiles by these LinkedIn industry IDs. Example: `4` for 'Software Development'. Full list: `https://github.com/HarvestAPI/linkedin-industry-codes-v2/blob/main/linkedin_industry_code_v2_all_eng_with_header.csv` |
| `maxItems` | integer |  |  | Maximum number of profiles to scrape — Maximum number of profiles to scrape. The actor will stop scraping when this limit is reached. |

## Output

The actor publishes no dataset schema, so `items` are untyped objects.
